legend: Enzo, a caveman, recently developed an interest in collecting stones as a hobby. He has a collection called A$$$A$$$ with N$$$N$$$ stones lined up in various colors and identified each color with an integer (for example, he defined color number 1$$$1$$$ as the color green).

The special aspect of his collection is that, for a given number x$$$x$$$, he is very particular about what he calls the "kuga-buga-x$$$x$$$ value"; this value is the number of colors that appear with a frequency that is a multiple of x$$$x$$$. For example, if he has 3$$$3$$$ yellow stones and 6$$$6$$$ blue stones, the kuga-buga-3$$$3$$$ value is 2$$$2$$$, since he has two colors that appear a number of times that is a multiple of 3$$$3$$$.

Since he always wants to maintain the same number of stones but wants to keep the collection up to date, he frequently replaces stones he no longer likes with a new one of another color. He calls this update a type 1$$$1$$$ query.
From time to time, he wonders about the kuga-buga value for a given number x$$$x$$$. He calls this question a type 2$$$2$$$ query.
With that, Enzo wants your help to answer these kuga-buga queries given the stone collection A$$$A$$$ and the updates that occur over time.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers N$$$N$$$ (1≤N≤3⋅105)$$$(1 \leq N \leq 3 \cdot 10^5)$$$ and Q$$$Q$$$ (1≤Q≤105)$$$(1 \leq Q \leq 10^5)$$$, the size of Enzo's collection and the number of queries, respectively.
The second line contains N$$$N$$$ integers Ai$$$A_i$$$ (1≤Ai≤106)$$$(1 \leq A_i \leq 10^6)$$$; the i$$$i$$$-th of these is the color of the stone at the i$$$i$$$-th position of A$$$A$$$.
The next Q$$$Q$$$ lines each contain a query.

A query can have one of two forms: "1$$$1$$$ i$$$i$$$ y$$$y$$$" (1≤i≤N, 1≤y≤106)$$$(1 \leq i \leq N,\ 1 \leq y \leq 10^6)$$$ (replace the i$$$i$$$-th stone with one of color y$$$y$$$) or "2$$$2$$$ x$$$x$$$" (1≤x≤106)$$$(1 \leq x \leq 10^6)$$$ (what is the kuga-buga-x$$$x$$$ value?).
output: For each query of type 2$$$2$$$, print the kuga-buga-x$$$x$$$ value for the given value of x$$$x$$$.
